uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of how fast UK consumer prices are rising. The Bank of England targets it at 2%, so it moves rate expectations and the pound; the September figure also sets benefit uprating.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: Economists have put a number on the UK's exposure to a US diesel ban: inflation of 5% if it goes ahead. This September reading shows how far prices had run before any such shock, and it sets the baseline any diesel effect would be measured against.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-10.recent: The committee meets between two data runs that pull opposite ways: September prices rose 3.7% over the year on gasoline, while the Labor Department counted 29,000 new jobs against 90,000 expected. Most officials expect another hike by year-end, and Trump's panel is weighing the removal of Governor Lisa Cook from the committee.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-10.recent: Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, after a hike the ECB called proportionate, with business activity at a 3½-year high. Wunsch says the bank will probably have to hike again and Simkus sees more tightening; Knot wants a mildly hawkish stance. Governments name Isabel Schnabel's successor by 28 October, the day before.

boj-2026-10.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-10.recent: Sources say the board may declare that underlying inflation has reached its 2% goal, the judgment any further tightening rests on. It meets with yen-priced imports costing 24.5% more than a year ago, and weeks after a global bond sell-off deepened as Japanese yields jumped.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-12.recent: Gasoline pushed US inflation to 3.7% in September while employers added only 29,000 jobs, so the committee weighs prices that have topped its target for 5.5 years against a stalling labour market. Officials are split over another hike, while Trump's panel weighs removing Governor Lisa Cook from the board that votes on it.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of leaders of the world's largest economies, hosted by the member holding the rotating presidency. Its members produce about 85% of global output, and its communiqué sets shared lines on trade and debt.
g20-2026-miami.recent: The US presidency has pushed to bring the G20 back to its original priorities, and Russia's sherpa has publicly backed that push. That makes this summit a test of how far the other members accept a narrower agenda, and of which items survive into the final communiqué.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Euro-zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September, nearly double the target, weeks after a hike officials called proportionate. Wunsch and Simkus have since argued for more tightening and Knot for a mildly hawkish stance, while governments nominate a successor to Isabel Schnabel by 28 October.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: This meeting settles where the Bank of England's policy rate stands going into the new year, for the mortgage holders and savers whose payments follow it.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-12.recent: Three sources say the Bank of Japan may declare that underlying inflation has reached its 2% goal, the judgement any further tightening rests on. Yen-priced import costs are up 24.5% on a year, and Japanese yields have already jumped. The board weighs whether that imported pressure has become Japan's own.

fred-us-ppi-2026-10-15.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly Producer Price Index, which tracks what US producers receive for their goods and services. It shows cost pressure before it reaches shop prices, and bond yields move with it.
fred-us-ppi-2026-10-15.recent: The Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the latest US PPI reading. It will show how far price pressure has built up in the supply chain before it reaches shoppers.

fred-us-retail-sales-2026-10-15.standing: The Census Bureau's monthly estimate of what US stores, restaurants and online sellers took in. Consumer spending is about two-thirds of the US economy, so the figure moves growth forecasts, Treasury yields and the dollar.
fred-us-retail-sales-2026-10-15.recent: The Census Bureau publishes US retail sales, settling how much consumers spent at retailers and restaurants last month. It is the first hard spending figure for the month.
